newsitem.title: SPAIN: CPI data may power 10-yr Sep bono future to 103.50.
newsitem.headline: CPI data may power 10-yr Sep bono future to 103.50.

text.p: Spurred on by tame Spanish August inflation data, domestic 10-year September bond futures may climb to around 103.50 from 103.15 now if key U.S. August inflation data permits, bond traders said on Friday.

"Seeing as we've never been at these levels, there is no key resistance level above here except maybe in psychological terms at 103.50. But if after good inflation data here, we see a good number out of the States, the road has been paved for us," said a bond strategist at a Spanish brokerage.
But dealers said investor interest was focused mainly on five-year government bonds, with some switching out of the shorter end of the curve.
Spanish inflation rose 0.3 percent in August from July, unchanged at 3.7 percent year-on-year. The data boosted government bond futures to new historic highs.

One trader said the better-than-expected domestic data may prompt the Bank of Spain to cut rates again, even before details are presented on the 1997 budget, a factor most see as key to the next cut in rates.
